**What changed:** In Angular 22.0.0, `stream` `Resource` (which includes `rxResource`) "are now resolving the value synchronously if the stream/observable returns a value sychronously. This can break some tests that assumed an asynchronous resolution of the value." ((https://github.com/angular/angular/releases/tag/v22.0.0) — listed under **Breaking Changes → core**.) Previously such resources resolved their value asynchronously; now, when the underlying observable emits synchronously (e.g. `of(...)`, a `BehaviorSubject`), the `Resource` signals `value` / `status` / `isLoading` / `hasValue` update immediately instead of after a microtask/tick ((https://v22.angular.dev/api/core/Resource) for the signal-based `Resource` API surface).

**Affects:** Applications and especially unit tests that use `stream` `Resource`s or `rxResource` with synchronously-emitting observables and relied on the value not being available until a later tick (e.g. asserting `isLoading`/`status` of `Loading` right after triggering, or reading the value only after `fixture.whenStable()`/`await`).

**Action:** required: re-verify tests and code that read `Resource` `value`/`status`/`isLoading` after synchronous-observable streams; update assertions that assumed asynchronous (microtask-delayed) resolution to expect the value immediately, or wrap reads in the same async barriers the test framework already uses.

**What changed:** Angular v22.0.0 introduced a breaking change in the `compiler`: "This change will trigger the `nullishCoalescingNotNullable` and `optionalChainNotNullable` diagnostics on exisiting projects. You might want to disable those 2 diagnotiscs in your `tsconfig` temporarily." (, also fetched via https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/22.0.x/CHANGELOG.md). These are Angular extended template type-check diagnostics reported for templates where a `??` (nullish coalescing) or `?.` (optional chain) is applied to an expression the template type checker already considers non-nullable, i.e. code that previously compiled silently now produces new compiler diagnostics. The v22.0.x changelog contains no further detail and no automated migration schematic for these two diagnostics (the listed v22 migrations, e.g. "Injectable to Service", are unrelated — https://angular.dev/reference/migrations).

**Affects:** Applications whose templates use `a ?? b` or `a?.b` on values typed as non-nullable, and that run template type checking (`fullTemplateTypeCheck`/`strictTemplates` or the default v22 type checker); the diagnostics surface at build/`ng build`, `ng test` and in the Angular Language Service.

**Action:** required: re-verify that the project builds after upgrading; fix the flagged template expressions (remove the redundant `??`/`?.` or correct the underlying nullability), or, as the release notes advise, temporarily disable the `nullishCoalescingNotNullable` and `optionalChainNotNullable` diagnostics in the project's `tsconfig` compiler options while the templates are cleaned up. Exact `tsconfig` key names for silencing them are not shown in the fetched pages.

**Before/after:**

```
# Angular v22 CHANGELOG, "Breaking Changes > compiler":
- This change will trigger the `nullishCoalescingNotNullable` and `optionalChainNotNullable` diagnostics on exisiting projects.
  You might want to disable those 2 diagnotiscs in your `tsconfig` temporarily.
```

**What changed:** The compiler no longer strips the `data-` prefix when parsing template attribute names. Previously `data-` attributes were treated as aliases that bound inputs, outputs, events, references, and template variables; now they are ordinary `TextAttribute` / `BoundAttribute` nodes with the literal `data-*` name preserved. Affected legacy syntaxes that stopped working: `data-bind-` (bound inputs), `data-on-` (bound events), `data-bindon-` (both bound attribute and bound event), `data-ref-` (references), and `data-let-` (template variables). The internal `normalizeAttributeName` helper was removed from `packages/compiler/src/render3/r3_template_transform.ts` so a binding like `
` now emits `BoundAttribute` keyed `data-prop` instead of `prop` (). The commit message states: "data prefixed attribute no-longer bind inputs nor outputs" and "If you want to bind a data attribute, use the `attr.` prefix (which was already supported)." It also closes long-standing issue angular/angular#26406, where `
` stripped `data-` and bound to `id` instead of the `data-id` attribute (). **Affects:** Templates that use any of the `data-` binding aliases: `data-bind-*`, `data-on-*`, `data-bindon-*`, `data-ref-*`, `data-let-*`, or that relied on the compiler stripping `data-` from a property binding to set an actual `data-*` HTML attribute. Language-service quick-info on those syntaxes is also affected. **Action:** required: in templates, replace legacy `data-` binding aliases with standard Angular binding syntax. Use `[foo]="..."` or `[(foo)]` for inputs, `(event)="..."` for outputs, `#name` for references, `let name` on structural directives for template variables, and the `attr.` prefix (e.g. `[attr.data-id]="..."`) when binding to a literal `data-*` attribute. Re-verify any component whose inputs/outputs were previously wired via `data-bind-`/`data-on-`/`data-bindon-` and re-check `*ngFor`/`*ngIf`/`*ngTemplateOutlet` templates that used `data-let-`. **Before/after:** ```html
{{hero}}
{{hero}}
```

**What changed:** In Angular 22.0.0 the `min` and `max` validation rules in `@angular/forms` "no longer support string values. Bound values must be numbers or null." (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/22.0.x/CHANGELOG.md, Breaking Changes → forms). The `MinValidator` and `MaxValidator` directives still declare their `@Input() min` / `@Input() max` as `string | number | null`, but validation now requires numeric bindings; passing a string is a behavioral break (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/22.0.x/packages/forms/src/directives/validators.ts). The changelog entry itself is truncated at "no longer support", so the precise new runtime semantics (whether string values now fail validation or throw) are not fully documented in the fetched sources.

**Affects:** Applications that bind a string value to the `min` or `max` attribute on a `type="number"` input associated with `formControlName`, `formControl`, or `ngModel` (the `MinValidator`/`MaxValidator` selector), or that pass string arguments to `Validators.min` / `Validators.max`.

**Action:** required: change string-bound `min`/`max` inputs to number bindings and re-verify the validation result of the affected controls, since the exact new behavior for string values is unclear from the sources.

**Before/after:**
```html
<!-- before: string bound -->
<input type="number" ngModel min="4">
<!-- after: bound as a number -->
<input type="number" ngModel [min]="4">
```

**What changed:** The `provideRoutes()` function from `@angular/router`, which had been deprecated since v15, has been removed from the public API in v22. The removal commit states: "`provideRoutes` was deprecated in v15. `provideRoutes()` has been removed. Use `provideRouter()` or `ROUTES` as multi token if necessary." (`https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/bdb6ae9`; commit titled "refactor(router): remove deprecated `provideRoutes` function.", authored by JeanMeche, committed by thePunderWoman on Feb 24, search index at `https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Aangular%2Fangular+provideRoutes+removed&type=commits`).

**Affects:** Applications that import and call `provideRoutes()` from `@angular/router` (typically inside `bootstrapApplication()` / `providers` arrays or feature provider factories) rather than `provideRouter()`.

**Action:** required: Remove all `provideRoutes()` imports and calls from `@angular/router`. Replace them with `provideRouter()`, or, when route definitions need to be registered through a multi-provider pattern, supply them via the `ROUTES` token as a multi token. Re-verify application and feature route registration after the swap. (Only the high-level replacement guidance is in the sources; concrete replacement snippets are not shown.)

**What changed:** Angular compiler expressions with optional chaining (`?.`) now return `undefined` when a step in the chain is null or undefined (previously returned `null`). To opt out of this behavior change, expressions can be wrapped with the `$null` magic function (e.g., `$null(foo?.bar?.baz)`) to restore the `null` behavior. (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/2896c93cc1077e1306acd91f4ed62fed4204a26b) **Affects:** Applications using Angular templates with expressions containing optional chaining operators. **Action:** required: Verify and update application logic that relies on the evaluation of expressions with optional chaining, specifically where code or bindings depend on a `null` value check following a failed navigation. Update templates to wrap expressions with `$null` to retain previous behavior if needed. **Before/after:** ```html
{{foo?.bar?.baz}}
{{foo?.bar?.baz}}
{{$null(foo?.bar?.baz)}}
```

**What changed:** The template compiler's HTML lexer (`packages/compiler/src/ml_parser/lexer.ts`, `_Tokenizer._consumeTagOpen`) now accepts C/JS-style inline comments inside an element's opening tag — between attributes, between `[input]`/`(output)` bindings, and just before `>` — where they previously caused parse errors. Two forms are supported: single-line `// comment` (new private `_consumeSingleLineComment`, consumed to end of line) and block `/* ... */` (`_consumeMultiLineComment`, may span lines, also handles `*` inside the comment). A commented-out attribute yields no attribute, e.g. `
` produces only `attr2`; attribute `sourceSpan` offsets stay correct. Tests: `packages/compiler/test/ml_parser/inline_comment_spec.ts`. The VS Code extension grammar was updated in the same commit: `vscode-ng-language-service/syntaxes/template-tag.json` gained `#inlineComments`, `#standardAttribute` and `#other` patterns, plus a new `angular-tag-comment` language with `syntaxes/template-tag-language-configuration.json` (`"blockComment": ["/*", "*/"]`) and `embeddedLanguages: {"template.tag.ng": "angular-tag-comment"}` in `vscode-ng-language-service/package.json` (commit e850643b1b8dca8cfdc12705be51441197cd987a). **Affects:** Applications that use (or will add) `//` or `/* */` comments inside opening tags. Purely additive: templates without such comments are unaffected. Note `//` at an attribute position is now always a comment start, so any attribute-looking text beginning with `//` there is no longer lexed as an attribute. **Action:** none — no code, configuration, or dependency changes are needed; optionally re-verify templates containing text starting with `//` in attribute position still parse as intended. **Before/after:** ```html
``` (`https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/e850643b1b8dca8cfdc12705be51441197cd987a`)

**What changed:** Angular's compiler no longer treats `data-` prefixed attributes as bindings to directive inputs or outputs. Previously, a template attribute like `<div data-id="{{1}}">` was interpreted as a binding to an input named `id` (with the `data-` prefix stripped), rather than as a plain HTML `data-*` attribute — this behaviour had been deprecated for a long time (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/488d962bc700fb7189749c63ba63eac50a54e363, https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/26406). Per the commit: "data prefixed attribute no-longer bind inputs nor outputs", and "If you want to bind a data attribute, use the `attr.` prefix (which was already supported)." The change was made to improve consistency and match developer expectations, resolving issue #26406 ("data- prefix gets stripped from bindings such as `<div data-id="{{1}}">`"), which was labelled `breaking changes`.

**Affects:** Templates that rely on `data-<name>` attribute syntax to bind a directive input or output (i.e. depending on the `data-` prefix being stripped and the remainder matched to an input/output name). Pure static `data-*` HTML attributes and attribute bindings written with the `attr.` prefix are unaffected.

**Action:** required: change any template bindings that used the `data-` prefix to reach a directive input/output — use the input name directly, e.g. `[id]="value"` — and use the `attr.` prefix (e.g. `[attr.data-id]="value"`) when the intent is to bind an HTML data attribute. Then re-verify templates containing `data-*` attributes with interpolations or property bindings for changed rendering.

**Before/after:**
```html
<div data-id="{{1}}">

<!-- bind the data attribute explicitly instead -->
<div [attr.data-id]="1">
```

**What changed:** A single PR (#68868) landed three commits in Angular 22.0.0 that fix security-context/schema lookups for namespaced tags: 1. `ab9154ab75` — `DomElementSchemaRegistry` (`packages/compiler/src/schema/dom_element_schema_registry.ts`) now runs tag names through a new `normalizeTagName()` helper that uses `splitNsName()` and strips any namespace other than the built-in `svg`/`math` ones. So `hasProperty`, `hasElement`, `securityContext`, `allKnownAttributesOfElement` and `allKnownEventsOfElement` query the schema with the simple tag name (`:xhtml:a` → `a`) instead of the full namespaced name, which previously fell through to `SecurityContext.NONE` and to the `unknown` property schema (`:xhtml:a|href` never matched `a|href`) (`https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/ab9154ab75bdd36759c77917216b57285b243ea4`, diff in `https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/68868`). 2. `6ff620a033` — `SECURITY_SCHEMA()` in both `packages/compiler/src/schema/dom_security_schema.ts` and `packages/core/src/sanitization/dom_security_schema.ts` now registers `href` and `xlink:href` on `a` under `SVG_NAMESPACE` as `SecurityContext.URL`, via `registerContext(SecurityContext.URL, SVG_NAMESPACE, [['a', ['href', 'xlink:href']]])`. Dynamic bindings on SVG links now compile to `ɵɵsanitizeUrl`, so e.g. `'javascript:alert(1)'` renders as `unsafe:javascript:alert(1)`. Static attribute values are unchanged/not sanitized (`https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/6ff620a03364d6ab60cea47de942a04ec5a26c50`). 3. `a08e4fb93c` — `i18nResolveSanitizer` in `packages/core/src/render3/i18n/i18n_parse.ts` normalizes the tag name the same way before the security-schema lookup, so translated attributes on custom-namespaced elements get the right sanitizer (`https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/a08e4fb93c371252da16b3b22cbf78f4ac180fa2`). **Affects:** (a) templates using elements in custom XML/XHTML namespaces (e.g. ``, `` via `xmlns:xhtml=...`) with property bindings or i18n'd attributes — these now receive URL/HTML sanitization they previously bypassed, and unknown-property/schema errors may now surface where the `unknown` schema used to apply; and (b) templates binding `[attr.href]` / `[attr.xlink:href]` on `

**What changed:** Angular's compiler no longer has dedicated handling for legacy Shadow DOM v0 selectors. `_shadowDOMSelectorsRe` and `_convertShadowDOMSelectors` were removed from `packages/compiler/src/shadow_css.ts`, so `::shadow`, `::content`, `/shadow-deep/`, and `/shadow/` are no longer treated specially or stripped from user CSS during component style scoping; they are now scoped like any standard selector (the component scope attribute is appended rather than the pseudo being converted/removed). A legacy failing test in `shadow_css_spec.ts` was also deleted. The remaining `ShadowCss.shimCssText` pipeline in `shadow_css.ts` now runs only `_insertPolyfillHostInCssText`, `_convertColonHost`, `_convertColonHostContext`, keyframe scoping and `_scopeSelectors` — the shadow-selector conversion step is gone (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/194f723f6620ea3cdf490b762ecbef8df6bb2c8a, confirmed against `shadow_css.ts` at that commit).

**Affects:** Applications whose component CSS (`@Component` `styles`/`styleUrls`, emulated encapsulation) still contains the deprecated legacy selectors `::shadow`, `::content`, `/shadow-deep/`, or `/shadow/`.

**Action:** required: remove or rewrite any component CSS rules using `::shadow`, `::content`, `/shadow-deep/`, or `/shadow/` — these are deprecated Shadow DOM v0 selectors and previously got converted/stripped by the compiler; they will now be emitted with the component scope attribute appended, changing (and typically breaking) the resulting CSS. Re-verify rendered styles for components containing such selectors.

**Before/after:**
```css
/* before: compiler converted/stripped these legacy selectors during scoping
   after: they are scoped like ordinary selectors, e.g. */
::content(.inner) { color: red; }   /* now scoped as a normal selector */
/shadow-deep/ .inner { color: red; }
```
*(no official before/after output snippet was available on the fetched pages; selector names above are quoted verbatim from the commit message)*

**What changed:** In Angular 22, `href` and `xlink:href` on SVG `<a>` elements were registered under `SecurityContext.URL` in the compiler and core DOM security schemas via `registerContext(SecurityContext.URL, SVG_NAMESPACE, [['a', ['href', 'xlink:href']]])` (i.e. schema keys `:svg:a|href` and `:svg:a|xlink:href`); previously these attribute/tag combos were unmapped, so dynamic bindings bypassed sanitization entirely and allowed `javascript:` URLs (XSS). The compiler now emits runtime URL sanitization (`ɵɵsanitizeUrl`) for these bindings (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/6ff620a03364d6ab60cea47de942a04ec5a26c50, https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/68868, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/6ff620a03364d6ab60cea47de942a04ec5a26c50/packages/compiler/src/schema/dom_security_schema.ts). Related fixes in the same PR: `DomElementSchemaRegistry` now normalizes custom-namespaced tag names (e.g. `:xhtml:a` → `a`, for namespaces other than the built-in `svg` and `math`) so lookups return `SecurityContext.URL` instead of `SecurityContext.NONE` (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/ab9154ab75bdd36759c77917216b57285b243ea4), and `i18nResolveSanitizer` normalizes namespaced tag names before security-context lookup (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/a08e4fb93c371252da16b3b22cbf78f4ac180fa2).

**Affects:** Templates with dynamic bindings to `href` or `xlink:href` on `<a>` inside SVG (`:svg:a`), and elements using custom XML/XHTML namespaces whose `href`-like attributes were previously unsanitized. Static (non-bound) values remain allowed.

**Action:** none — security fix applied automatically; applications that bound untrusted values (e.g. `javascript:` URLs) to these attributes will now have them sanitized/neutralized at runtime. Re-verify that any intentionally trusted SVG link values still render correctly, bypassing with `DomSanitizer` if needed.

**Before/after:**
```ts
// after (Angular 22) — compiler/core dom_security_schema.ts
registerContext(SecurityContext.URL, SVG_NAMESPACE, [['a', ['href', 'xlink:href']]]);
```

**What changed:** The Angular compiler no longer interprets `{{in}}` (and similar reserved-word-like expressions such as `typeof`) as string literals in template expressions. Previously, an expression like `{{ in }}` would resolve to the string `'in'` instead of accessing a component field or template variable named `in`. Now, referencing `in` as an identifier in an expression throws a compilation error. Template reference variables like `` remain valid, but using `{{in}}` in an interpolation or binding context that is ambiguous with a JavaScript/TypeScript reserved word or operator will fail (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/786ef8261f4faca0693ef73938d3a6275b5baf7f) (https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/65244). **Affects:** Applications that have template expressions referencing identifiers named `in` or other reserved keywords (e.g., `typeof`, `void`, `new`) that were previously silently resolved as string literals or operator tokens rather than component fields or template variables. **Action:** required: Update templates to use explicit `this.in` (if accessing a class field) or ensure template variables do not collide with reserved words. Re-verify any template expressions using identifiers that might be interpreted as operators. **Before/after:** ```html
{{in}}
{{ typeof }}
{{ this.in }}
```

**What changed:** The Angular Ivy compilation transform (`IvyTransformationVisitor` in `packages/compiler-cli/src/ngtsc/transform/src/transform.ts`) previously re-created `ts.PropertyDeclaration` nodes passing only `node.questionToken`, which silently dropped TypeScript's `exclamationToken` — i.e. the definite-assignment `!` modifier — from class properties. The fix changes the argument to `node.questionToken || node.exclamationToken`, so `!` properties are now preserved through the transform (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/7a0d6b8df21ca6a407e5c63dc0af753bc39c90c5 and its patch).

**Affects:** Applications whose code (or generated/downleveled code processed by the Ivy transform, e.g. language-level downleveling) declares class properties with the definite assignment assertion, e.g. `foo!: string;`, and relies on the emitted/transformed output retaining it.

**Action:** none — this is an internal compiler-cli correctness fix; no application code, configuration, or dependency changes are required. Applications that previously worked around the dropped `!` may re-verify that behavior.

**Before/after:**
```ts
// transform.ts, IvyTransformationVisitor — before
node.questionToken,
// after
node.questionToken || node.exclamationToken,
```

**What changed:** A new extended diagnostic `NG8023` was introduced in `@angular/compiler-cli` (commit `ca67828ee2`) to report duplicate component selectors during compilation. This replaces the former runtime error `NG0300`, shifting the failure detection from runtime to build time. Elements with multiple matching selectors will now throw at compile time instead of runtime. (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/ca67828ee247bdff46736661e51f43f2ca736a24, https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/48377)

**Affects:** Applications where components or directives share identical or overlapping selectors that result in multiple components matching the same element. (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/ca67828ee247bdff46736661e51f43f2ca736a24)

**Action:** required: Re-verify component and directive selectors for uniqueness or proper exclusivity. Update code to resolve any duplicate selector conflicts that previously triggered a runtime `NG0300` error, as these will now fail the build with `NG8023`. (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/ca67828ee247bdff46736661e51f43f2ca736a24)

**What changed:** Angular 22 adds a new stable-surface core API `provideWebMcpTools`, exported from `@angular/core` (via the `webmcp` entry, alongside the existing `declareWebMcpTool` and the types `WebMcpToolExecute`, `WebMcpClient`, `WebMcpToolDescriptor`) (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/3b0ae5fef0328477ee0f5d51980217e7c583a606/packages/core/src/webmcp/index.ts, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/3b0ae5fef0328477ee0f5d51980217e7c583a606/packages/core/src/core.ts). It is an ergonomic wrapper around `declareWebMcpTool` that lets a user define multiple Web MCP tools directly in an injector's `providers` array, instead of needing an injection context. The tool's `execute` function runs in the injection context of the `Injector` the provider is given to, so it can `inject` dependencies. It combines with route `providers` plus `withExperimentalAutoCleanupInjectors` so tools register on navigation to a route and are unregistered on navigating away; the commit notes `withExperimentalAutoCleanupInjectors` is required for unregistration to work (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/3b0ae5fef0328477ee0f5d51980217e7c583a606).

**Affects:** Applications using Web MCP tool registration (`declareWebMcpTool`), or opting in to Web MCP tools in Angular 22. Additive feature — existing code is not broken.

**Action:** none (optional: adopt `provideWebMcpTools` in `providers` for multi-tool registration; when registering via route `providers`, add `withExperimentalAutoCleanupInjectors` to get automatic unregistration on navigation away).

**Before/after:**
No fetched page contained a runnable code snippet (the commit's examples were elided), so none is reproduced here. Public exports added, per the source: `export {provideWebMcpTools} from './provide_tools';`

**What changed:** `ApplicationRef.bootstrap` was extended to align its shape with the `createComponent` function, accepting a config object (directives, bindings, etc.) as its second argument instead of only a host element / `BootstrapOptions` (angular.dev/api/core/BootstrapOptions is now deprecated in favor of providers) (commit a0aa8304cd78a58a990c3b648e41f6888b50b1b3, issue #67946). The breaking part: "The second argument of `appRef.bootstrap` does not accept `any` anymore. Make sure the element you pass is not nullable." Previously the second parameter was loosely typed (an element, selector, or `BootstrapOptions` object, effectively `any`); now the argument is strictly typed, so passing a possibly-null value such as the result of `document.querySelector(...)` no longer type-checks (#67946, commit a0aa8304cd). The old signature remains partly for backwards compatibility: the first argument still accepts a Component type or a component factory (#67946).

**Affects:** Applications that call `appRef.bootstrap(...)` (e.g. from an `ngDoBootstrap` hook) with a second argument whose type is not narrowed — notably nullable results like `document.querySelector('app-root')`, `ElementRef.nativeElement` typed loosely, or values typed `any`/`Element|null`.

**Action:** required: re-verify all `ApplicationRef.bootstrap` call sites with a second argument; narrow or assert non-null (e.g. `document.querySelector('app-root')!` or an explicit `if (el)` guard) so the passed element is non-nullable, and adapt code where the second argument previously relied on `any`-typed `BootstrapOptions`-style objects. Applications only using `bootstrapApplication` or `platformBrowserDynamic().bootstrapModule` are unaffected.

Before/after: no code snippet was available in the fetched pages.

**What changed:** Angular 22 drops TypeScript 5.9 support; only TypeScript 6.0 is now supported (`>=6.0 <6.1`). In the commit, `@angular/compiler-cli`'s peerDependency on `typescript` was changed from `"typescript": ">=5.9 <6.1"` to `"typescript": ">=6.0 <6.1"`, and the compiler's internal constant in `packages/compiler-cli/src/typescript_support.ts` was raised from `MIN_TS_VERSION = '5.9.0'` to `MIN_TS_VERSION = '6.0.0'`; the `verifySupportedTypeScriptVersion`/`checkVersion` path throws `The Angular Compiler requires TypeScript >=<min> and <max> but <version> was found instead.` when the installed compiler is out of range (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/8fe025f5149d7eb460e784a5a17bb467f85b9080). The repo also removed its `integration/typings_test_ts59` type-check project, which pinned `"typescript": "6.0.2"` (same commit).

**Affects:** Applications that pin or resolve `typescript` at 5.9.x (or any version < 6.0) while using `@angular/compiler-cli` 22.0.0 — including builds through the Angular CLI, `ng-packagr`, or direct `ngc`/`tsc -p` type-checking.

**Action:** required: bump the `typescript` devDependency to a 6.0.x release (the Angular 22 peer range is `>=6.0 <6.1`; e.g. `6.0.2`, as used in the removed Angular integration test) and re-run `ng build`/`ng test` to confirm type-checking succeeds. Review `tsconfig.json` compiler options only if the TypeScript 6.0 upgrade surfaces new diagnostics.

**Before/after:**
```jsonc
// packages/compiler-cli/package.json — peerDependencies
-    "typescript": ">=5.9 <6.1"
+    "typescript": ">=6.0 <6.1"
```
```ts
// packages/compiler-cli/src/typescript_support.ts
-const MIN_TS_VERSION = '5.9.0';
+const MIN_TS_VERSION = '6.0.0';
```
(https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/8fe025f5149d7eb460e784a5a17bb467f85b9080)

**What changed:** `enableProfiling()` (Chrome DevTools performance integration in `packages/core/src/render3/debug/chrome_dev_tools_performance.ts`) now passes a 7th `detail` argument to `console.timeStamp` of the form `{description: 'Documentation', url: docUrl}`, so DevTools performance markers deep-link to Angular docs. URLs are built from `VERSION` — `<major>.angular.dev` for stable releases, `` for `-next`/`-rc` builds. Mapping: `ProfilerEvent.ChangeDetectionStart`/`ChangeDetectionEnd`/`ChangeDetectionSyncStart`/`ChangeDetectionSyncEnd` → `/best-practices/runtime-performance`; `AfterRenderHooksStart`/`AfterRenderHooksEnd` → `/guide/components/lifecycle#aftereveryrender-and-afternextrender`; `DeferBlockStateStart`/`DeferBlockStateEnd` → `/guide/defer`; `LifecycleHookStart` → `/guide/components/lifecycle#<hookname>` (lowercased, e.g. `#ngoninit`). The `console.timeStamp` global declaration gained an optional `detail?: object` parameter; the `assertEqual` import was dropped. The commit message notes the panel rendering "Requires: chrome://flags/#enable-devtools-deep-link-via-extensibility-api" (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/2f5ab541eafba72bc0079a8650d0b96b0ddfde2f and its .patch).

**Affects:** Only applications calling `enableProfiling()` and inspecting `console.timeStamp` profiler output; no application code, config, or dependency change. The new detail data is only visible in DevTools when the experimental flag is enabled.

**Action:** none

**Before/after:**

**What changed:** Nested leave animations are re-introduced in Angular 22.0.0 (commit df659b8d0cf64eeed418c60bc16cae5630086401, https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/df659b8d0cf64eeed418c60bc16cae5630086401). Previously `animate.leave` was strict: "leave animations only happen on the node being removed. No animations are triggered for elements that are children of the node being removed" (https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/67633). Now the engine waits for nested inner `animate.leave` transitions natively, but only when they exist within the same component's view or its embedded tracking structures (like `@if` and `@for`). The commit explicitly marks: "Breaking: Leave animations are no longer limited to the element being removed." The scoping to component boundaries was added specifically so that removal of a parent component or route navigation does not traverse into child component views waiting for their `animate.leave` animations, which "would excessively stall" navigations and parental destruction (commit page). Per issue #67633, the goal was that "child animations fire scoped within the template of the component being removed, and do not cross component boundaries." **Affects:** Applications using `@if`/`@for` (or other embedded views) around elements with `animate.leave` transitions inside a component's own template, and applications relying on the previous strict behavior where child `animate.leave` animations never ran when an ancestor node was removed; also apps whose animation-completion timing/donut tests assume only the removed node animates. **Action:** required: re-verify leave-animation behavior in component templates that wrap animated children in `@if`/`@for` — child `animate.leave` transitions inside the same component view now actually run and delay element removal until they complete, while animations in child components are still not waited on across component boundaries (route navigation and parent destruction timing should be checked for changes). **Before/after:** ```html @if (show) {
...
} ```

**What changed:** In `@angular/core/testing`, the `TestBed` static method `getFixture<T = unknown>(): ComponentFixture<T>` was renamed to `getLastFixture<T = unknown>(): ComponentFixture<T>` in the `TestBed` interface and `TestBedImpl` (goldens: `packages/core/testing/index.api.md`) (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/dc3131c639542ad6a463bff3da5ca84c6f8ecb6f). Use TestBed.createComponent and store the fixture on the test context, rather than using TestBed.getFixture."` when more than one active fixture existed; now it returns the most recently created fixture (`this._activeFixtures[this._activeFixtures.length - 1]`) with no error for multiple fixtures. It still throws `"No fixture has been created yet."` when none exists (e.g. after `TestBed.resetTestingModule()`). Angular's internal helper `expectText` in `packages/private/testing/src/utils.ts` now calls `TestBed.getLastFixture().nativeElement`.

**Affects:** Tests that call `TestBed.getFixture()` (including code relying on the multi-fixture error).

**Action:** required: rename every `TestBed.getFixture()` call to `TestBed.getLastFixture()`. Re-verify tests that created multiple fixtures via `TestBed.createComponent()` and previously expected a thrown error — the call now silently returns the last created fixture instead.

**Before/after:**

// after (Angular 22.0)
const fixture = TestBed.getLastFixture(); // returns most recently created fixture

**What changed:** PR #68868 (three commits) fixed security-context lookup for namespaced/SVG elements. (1) `fix(core)` — namespaced tag names (e.g. `:xhtml:a` → `a`) are now normalized inside `i18nResolveSanitizer` before looking up the security context, so custom namespaced tag attributes get correct translation sanitization at runtime (a08e4fb). (2) `fix(compiler)` — `DomElementSchemaRegistry` now normalizes tag names for custom namespaces (other than the built-in `svg` and `math` namespaces) to their simple HTML counterparts for all registry queries; previously the full namespaced name (e.g. `:xhtml:a`) bypassed the `a|href` sanitization registry and returned `SecurityContext.NONE` instead of `SecurityContext.URL` (ab9154a). (3) `fix(compiler)` — `href` and `xlink:href` on SVG `<a>` elements are now registered under `SecurityContext.URL` in both the compiler and core DOM security schemas, so template compilation emits runtime `ɵɵsanitizeUrl` on these attributes; previously they were unmapped and bypassed sanitization entirely, an XSS risk with untrusted input such as `javascript:` URLs (6ff620a). Static values are still allowed. (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/68868)

**Affects:** applications that (a) bind `href`/`xlink:href` on SVG `<a>` elements (`<svg><a [href]="...">`), (b) use custom XML/XHTML-namespaced elements such as `<xhtml:a>` with bound properties, or (c) use runtime i18n with attributes on namespaced tags.

**Action:** none — this is a security hardening fix, no code or configuration change is required. Required only in the sense of behaviour to re-verify: dynamic `href`/`xlink:href` values on SVG `<a>` that previously passed through unsanitized (e.g. `javascript:` or otherwise unsafe URLs) will now be sanitized/rejected at runtime, and namespaced-tag attribute bindings now receive `SecurityContext.URL` sanitization instead of `NONE`.

**What changed:** Signal Forms (`@angular/forms/signals`) now allow binding a `number | null` model directly to `<input type="text">` (and to a bare `<input>` with no `type`) via `[formField]`, instead of requiring `<input type="number">` or a custom control (fixes #66903 and #66157) (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/41b1410cb8a333a2ce6569483cd10866effc154d). Runtime behaviour, implemented in `getNativeControlValue`/`setNativeControlValue` in `packages/forms/signals/src/directive/native.ts`: numeric model values are rendered via `String(value)` (`NaN` renders as `''`), `null` renders as `''`; when typing, `''` becomes `null`, other input is `Number(...)`-parsed, and a non-numeric value raises a parse error (`NativeInputParseError`, error `kind: 'parse'`, model value left unchanged) (patch, https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/41b1410cb8a333a2ce6569483cd10866effc154d.patch). Template type-checking in `TcbNativeFieldOp` (compiler-cli `ngtsc/typecheck/src/ops/signal_forms.ts`) changed: text-like inputs are no longer typed as plain `string`; they now use an invariant union check `{ (): string; set: (v: string) => void; } | { (): number | null; set: (v: number | null) => void; }`, so only `Field<string>` or `Field<number|null>` are accepted — `Field<number>` (without `null`), `string | null`, and `boolean` fields are now rejected on text/bare inputs. Separately, `<input type="radio">` now expects `string` (previously the fallback).

**Affects:** Applications using Signal Forms (`form()` from `@angular/forms/signals`, `FormField` directive) that bind `number`/`number | null` models to `<input type="text">` or `<input>` without a `type`; previously such code failed template type-checking and would now compile and behave numerically. Also newly type-rejected: numeric (non-nullable) models on bare/text inputs.

**Action:** none — this is an additive feature; no code must change to upgrade. Optionally, migrate numeric editing off `<input type="number">` to `<input type="text" inputmode="numeric">` bound to a `number | null` signal model; re-verify any existing templates where a `number` (non-nullable) model is bound to a text/bare input, since these are now type errors.

**Before/after:**
```html
<!-- Before: required type="number" (or a custom directive) for a numeric model -->
<input type="number" [formField]="f.age">

<!-- After (22.0): number|null models work on text inputs -->
<input type="text" inputmode="numeric" [formField]="f.age">
```
```ts
// from the commit's tests
readonly data = signal<number | null>(42);
readonly f = form(this.data); // <input type="text" [formField]="f"/> now type-checks
```

**What changed:** Angular 22 adds an `ngNoCva` attribute usable as an opt-out from the framework's built-in ControlValueAccessor directives. The selectors of `DefaultValueAccessor`, `CheckboxControlValueAccessor`, `NumberValueAccessor`, `RadioControlValueAccessor`, `RangeValueAccessor`, `SelectControlValueAccessor` and `SelectMultipleControlValueAccessor` now include a `:not([ngNoCva])` negative selector term, e.g. `DefaultValueAccessor`'s selector changed from `input:not([type=checkbox])[formControlName],textarea[formControlName],...,[ngDefaultControl]` to `input:not([type=checkbox]):not([ngNoCva])[formControlName],textarea:not([ngNoCva])[formControlName],...,[ngDefaultControl]` (the `[ngDefaultControl]` selector was left unchanged) (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/3983080236e348ecc17ab4e65a6a5cc0a16aa315.patch). Per the commit message, "If `FormsModule` or `ReactiveFormsModule` is present in the scope of a template, plain `<input>` and other form elements will get default CVA directives added. This commit adds an `ngNoCva` attribute as a negative selector for those directives, so `<input ngNoCva>` elements will not have them matched" (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/3983080236e348ecc17ab4e65a6a5cc0a16aa315). No new public class/export appears in the `goldens/public-api/forms/index.api.md` golden — only the directives' `ɵdir` selector strings changed.

**Affects:** Nothing existing breaks; purely additive. Relevant only for applications that previously had to work around automatic CVA matching (e.g. a custom third-party CVA or a hand-rolled value handling on `input`/`textarea`/`select` bound with `ngModel`, `formControl` or `formControlName`).

**Action:** none — existing templates are unaffected. Optionally, replace prior workarounds with `ngNoCva` on elements bound via `ngModel` / `formControl` / `formControlName` to stop the built-in accessors from matching. Note `ngNoCva` does not opt out of the `[ngDefaultControl]` selector of `DefaultValueAccessor`.

**Before/after:**
```html
<!-- before: built-in CVA always matched -->
<input type="text" [ngModel]="value" />

<!-- after (Angular 22): built-in CVAs are skipped via the ngNoCva negative selector -->
<input type="text" ngNoCva [ngModel]="value" />
```

**What changed:** Angular 22.0.0 added internal integration between form directives and `FormUiComponent` (FVC) signal-based form controls. `NgModel`, `FormControlDirective`, and `FormControlName` now emit `ɵngControlCreate` and `ɵngControlUpdate` lifecycle hooks, choose between the `ControlValueAccessor` (CVA) path and the FVC path based on the host element's capabilities, and add compiler-level specialization of control properties (`formControl`, `formControlName`, `ngModel`) via `ɵɵcontrolCreate()` and `ɵɵcontrol()` calls in compiled templates (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/c4ce3f345fdb14595f0991dff488c4043a0fc71c.patch). `NgModel` also exposes a new protected getter `shouldBindRequired`, and the compiler pipeline now recognizes these as eligible control properties for specialization.

**Affects:** Applications using a custom directive that acts as a `ControlValueAccessor` assigned via DI on elements also bound with `formControl`, `formControlName`, or `ngModel`; also applications defining custom components with both FVC-style signal inputs (e.g. `value`, `disabled`, `touched`) and CVA, since branching logic may now prefer the FVC path over CVA.

**Action:** required: re-verify that any custom `ControlValueAccessor` directives assigned via DI on elements bound with `formControl`, `formControlName`, or `ngModel` still receive `writeValue`, `registerOnChange`, and `registerOnTouched` calls as before; the commit states graceful fallback to CVA when no FVC pattern is detected, but custom implementations that partially mimic FVC signal inputs may be routed to the new path. Also re-verify that directives using `ngModel` with `required` attribute still work, since `NgModel` now uses `shouldBindRequired` internally.

**Before/after:**
```html
<!-- Before and after: template code is unchanged -->
<my-fvc-input [formControl]="ctrl" />

<!-- Before: compiled output did not include controlCreate/control calls -->
<!-- After: compiled output includes: -->
$r3$.ɵɵcontrolCreate();
$r3$.ɵɵcontrol();
```
Source: https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/c4ce3f345fdb14595f0991dff488c4043a0fc71c.patch

**What changed:** The signals-forms `FormField` directive (`[formField]`, from `packages/forms/signals`) now selects its `ControlValueAccessor` using the same precedence logic as standard reactive/template-driven forms. Previously, `FormField.controlValueAccessor` took the first entry of the injected `NG_VALUE_ACCESSOR` list (`this.controlValueAccessors?.[0]`) before falling back to the interop `NgControl`'s accessor. It now calls the internal `selectValueAccessor` helper exported from `@angular/forms` as `ɵselectValueAccessor`, which prefers a *custom* accessor, then a built-in accessor (subclass of `BuiltInControlValueAccessor`), then `DefaultValueAccessor` (`ngDefaultControl`), and throws in dev mode if more than one custom or more than one built-in accessor matches. The helper's signature also widened its second parameter to `readonly ControlValueAccessor[] | null | undefined` (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/de56d74da39178308b81a2d94c8eb4488cb0cbab).

**Affects:** Applications using the signals-forms `[formField]` directive on a host element where more than one `NG_VALUE_ACCESSOR` provider is present — e.g. a component with a custom `NG_VALUE_ACCESSOR` plus the built-in accessors or `ngDefaultControl` — and whose previously-picked (first-injection-order) accessor was not the custom one.

**Action:** required: re-verify value read/write and disabled-state behaviour of custom `ControlValueAccessor` components bound with `[formField]`; no code or dependency change is specified. Where the old code silently used the first registered accessor, the new code may pick a different accessor or throw a dev-mode error ("More than one custom value accessor matches form control with…") for ambiguous configurations.

**Before/after:**
```diff
-    return this.controlValueAccessors?.[0] ?? this.interopNgControl?.valueAccessor ?? undefined;
+    if (!this.controlValueAccessors || this.controlValueAccessors.length === 0) {
+      return this.interopNgControl?.valueAccessor ?? undefined;
+    }
+
+    // Rely on the exact logic in `@angular/forms` to pick the accessors with correct priority,
+    // passing our fake `InteropNgControl` to fulfill its first parameter requirement.
+    return (
+      selectValueAccessor(
+        this.interopNgControl as unknown as NgControl,
+        this.controlValueAccessors,
+      ) ?? undefined
+    );
```

**What changed:** The `touched` property, which previously could be used as a two-way binding, was split. The `touched` input represents the touched state of the field, while a new `touch` output allows a control implementation to indicate *when* the bound field is touched. Previously, a control could dictate that a field is no longer touched by setting `touched` to false; this behavior is disallowed now. ([commit fb166772d2](https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/fb166772d2e987c0145bdd5bbe83b2a29d74f31c))
**Affects:** Custom `ControlValueAccessor` implementations that previously used two-way binding (`[(touched)]`) or attempted to set the `touched` property to `false`.
**Action:** required: Change two-way bindings on `touched` to one-way input binding `[touched]` and add a new output binding `(touch)="...".` Update custom `ControlValueAccessor` code to trigger the `touch` event when the field is touched, rather than setting a boolean.
**Before/after:**
```html
<!-- Before -->
<my-custom-control [(touched)]="myForm.controls.name.touched" />

<!-- After -->
<my-custom-control [touched]="myForm.controls.name.touched" (touch)="markAsTouched()" />
```

**What changed:** In CVA (ControlValueAccessor) interop mode, `NgControl` now exposes `controlValue()` instead of `value()`, so custom controls bound through a CVA see the most recent user input immediately "rather than waiting for it to be synchronized after debouncing" (i.e. before the signal form's debounced model synchronization) (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/72d3ace03c1292ba9d6fdf7b418ba3287bf54316). The same PR (#67943, "Support NG_VALIDATORS in CVA mode", merged as a major-target feature) also shims legacy `NG_VALIDATORS` into signal-form parse errors: `NG_VALIDATORS` is injected into `FormField` and exposed via an internal getter; a `computed` signal in `cvaControlCreate` runs legacy validators and maps results into standard validation errors; and `registerOnValidatorChange` is intercepted so revalidation fires even when the model value is unchanged (e.g. `null` → `null`) (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/67943, https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/f9f24fc6699b762d17127d0412343041ecdea70e). On the reactive side, `NgControl.setParseErrorSource` converts a `Signal<ReadonlyArray<ParseError>>` (provided via `ɵFORM_FIELD_PARSE_ERRORS`, exposed as `NG_CONTROL_PARSE_ERRORS_PROVIDER`) into a validator that is added/removed on the `AbstractControl` and revalidated with `updateValueAndValidity({emitEvent: false})` (packages/forms/src/directives/ng_control.ts at the target commit).

**Affects:** Applications using signal forms (`@angular/forms/signals`) together with legacy reactive-form custom components that implement `ControlValueAccessor` and/or provide synchronous/async validators via `NG_VALIDATORS` — such components now receive the raw pre-debounce input value and their validators now feed signal-form error state.

**Action:** none (behavioral change; re-verify custom CVA components and `NG_VALIDATORS`-based validators under signal forms for timing differences — code that assumed `NgControl.value` was the debounced model value, or that assumed legacy validators were ignored in CVA mode, may need review).

**Before/after:** *(no code/configuration snippet showing old vs. new form appears in the fetched pages; the change is internal to `@angular/forms`.)*

**What changed:** The default `HttpBackend` implementation in `@angular/common/http` was switched from `HttpXhrBackend` to `FetchBackend` — `NG_DEFAULT_HTTP_BACKEND` in `packages/common/http/src/backend-default-value.ts` now resolves to `FetchBackend` instead of `HttpXhrBackend` (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/5c432fb8bb69343ef2633811c37c0c6c0fd65126). Because `FetchBackend` does not emit upload progress events, `HttpRequest.reportProgress` for uploads no longer reports progress by default; the docs in `request.ts` state: "The default `HttpBackend` based on fetch, does not support progress report for uploads. Set the `HttpXhrBackend` with `withXhr()` if you need this feature." XHR behaviour is restored by passing `withXhr()` to `provideHttpClient()`. `withFetch()` is now marked `@deprecated` ("`withFetch` is not required anymore. `FetchBackend` is the default `HttpBackend`.") and can be safely removed (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/5c432fb8bb69343ef2633811c37c0c6c0fd65126).

**Affects:** Applications calling `provideHttpClient()` without a backend feature and relying on upload progress events (`reportProgress: true` with uploads, `HttpEvent`/`HttpProgressEvent` for `HttpEventType.Sent`/upload progress); also applications that call the now-deprecated `withFetch()`; applications on the server that previously got a `console.warn` about `fetch` not being enabled.

**Action:** required: for upload progress support, add `withXhr()` to `provideHttpClient(...)`; remove deprecated `withFetch()` calls from `provideHttpClient(...)`; re-verify error/response behaviour of `HttpClient` requests previously relying on XHR specifics.

**Before/after:**
```ts
// Before (upload progress worked with XHR default; fetch required opt-in)
providers: [provideHttpClient(withFetch())]

// After (fetch is default; withFetch deprecated; XHR is now the opt-in)
providers: [provideHttpClient()]              // FetchBackend, no upload progress
providers: [provideHttpClient(withXhr())]     // HttpXhrBackend, upload progress
```
